old: Sahil bends a wire of length 96 cm, with nothing left over, to make the 12 edges of a cube. He then covers all six faces of the cube with paper. What area of paper does he use?
new: Sahil cuts a wire of length 96 cm into 12 equal pieces and uses them as the 12 edges of a cube. He then covers all six faces of the cube with paper. What area of paper does he use?
why: One unbroken wire cannot be bent to trace all 12 edges of a cube once each (8 odd-degree corners); cutting into 12 equal pieces is physically correct and states equal edges
